newsitem.title: UK: Youth to lead Asian demand for Western goods - report.
newsitem.headline: Youth to lead Asian demand for Western goods - report.

text.p: Asia is expected to remain the world's fastest growing regional market over the next 10 years, with an increasingly affluent youth driving the demand for Western-style consumer goods, according to a research report published on Tuesday.

Western culture is influencing virtually all walks of life, including eating habits, with the traditional rice-based Asian diet undergoing change, Euromonitor, a market research group said. In Japan per capita consumption of rice fell to about 66 kilograms in 1994 from 70 kilograms in 1990.

Euromonitor said it expects per capita consumption of rice in Korea to fall to 100 kg in the year 2000 from 107 kg in 1996. In Indonesia it sees rice consumption falling to 113 kg per person in the year 2000 from 111 kg in 1996.

There is growing demand for Western style foods, such as milk, cheese, eggs, bread and bakery products. The trend is particularly reflected in the growing popularity of Western fast food restaurant chains, especially U.S. hamburger and pizza restaurants, Euromonitor said.

Alchohol consumption is increasing in most Asian countries. Euromonitor said it foresees per capita alcohol consumption in Japn increasing to 87 litres in 2000 from 83 litres in 1996; in Taiwain increasing to 44 litres in 2000 from 40 litres in 1996; in Vietdnam to 5.8 litres isn 2000 from 4.3 litres in 1996, and in Indonesia increasing to 2.7 litres in 2000 from 1.5 litres in 1996.
